microtheory.name: logic_foundation
microtheory.definition: Formal logic as the substrate's reasoning foundation. Propositional + predicate + modal + nonclassical logics. Inference rules, proof, soundness, completeness, decidability. The substrate has math (which includes some logic) but lacks dedicated logic vocabulary at the level needed for its derivation_mechanism. Substrate analogue: the substrate's reasoning IS logical inference over its Concept graph.

concepts.name: proposition
concepts.definition: Truth-bearer. Either true or false. Substrate analogue: substrate's truth-assignable structure.

concepts.name: argument_logical
concepts.definition: Sequence of propositions: premises + conclusion. Substrate analogue: substrate's derivation chain.

concepts.name: validity_argument
concepts.definition: Argument structurally guaranteeing conclusion if premises true. Substrate analogue: substrate's structurally-sound inference.

concepts.name: soundness_argument
concepts.definition: Valid + premises actually true. Conclusion must be true. Substrate analogue: substrate's grounded valid inference.

concepts.name: inference_rule
concepts.definition: Pattern for deriving conclusion from premises. Modus ponens, modus tollens, etc. Substrate analogue: substrate's Rule pattern.

concepts.name: deductive_reasoning
concepts.definition: Premises guarantee conclusion. From general to specific. Substrate analogue: substrate's necessary inference.

concepts.name: inductive_reasoning
concepts.definition: Premises probabilify conclusion. From specific to general. Substrate analogue: substrate's empirical generalization.

concepts.name: abductive_reasoning
concepts.definition: Peirce. Inference to best explanation. From data to most plausible hypothesis. Substrate analogue: substrate's best-fit-hypothesis selection.

concepts.name: analogical_reasoning
concepts.definition: Mapping structure between domains. Substrate analogue: substrate's analogical_transfer faculty.

concepts.name: truth_value
concepts.definition: True or false. Classical logic: bivalent. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ-binary version.

concepts.name: bivalence_principle
concepts.definition: Every proposition is either true or false. Excluded middle. Substrate analogue: substrate's binary commitment principle.

concepts.name: many_valued_logic
concepts.definition: More than two truth values. Łukasiewicz. Substrate analogue: substrate's continuous σ values.

concepts.name: logical_connective
concepts.definition: Operators combining propositions: AND, OR, NOT, IF-THEN, IFF. Substrate analogue: substrate's Boolean Term-tree primitives.

concepts.name: conjunction_logic
concepts.definition: AND. True iff both true. Substrate analogue: substrate's And Term.

concepts.name: disjunction_logic
concepts.definition: OR. True iff at least one true. Inclusive vs exclusive. Substrate analogue: substrate's Or Term.

concepts.name: negation_logic
concepts.definition: NOT. Flips truth value. Substrate analogue: substrate's Not Term.

concepts.name: implication_logic
concepts.definition: IF-THEN. False only when antecedent true + consequent false. Material vs strict. Substrate analogue: substrate's rule head→body.

concepts.name: biconditional_logic
concepts.definition: IFF. True when both have same truth value. Substrate analogue: substrate's equivalence relation.

concepts.name: quantifier
concepts.definition: FORALL (∀) or EXISTS (∃). Bind variables ranging over domain. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-traversal scope.

concepts.name: universal_quantifier
concepts.definition: ∀x P(x). For all x, P holds. Substrate analogue: substrate's all-Mts iteration.

concepts.name: existential_quantifier
concepts.definition: ∃x P(x). Some x makes P hold. Substrate analogue: substrate's some-Mt finder.

concepts.name: tautology
concepts.definition: Proposition true in all interpretations. P ∨ ¬P. Substrate analogue: substrate's necessary truth.

concepts.name: contradiction_logic
concepts.definition: Always false. P ∧ ¬P. Substrate analogue: substrate's necessary falsehood.

concepts.name: contingency
concepts.definition: Sometimes true, sometimes false. Substrate analogue: substrate's empirical claim.

concepts.name: logical_equivalence
concepts.definition: Two propositions with same truth value in all interpretations. P ↔ Q tautological. Substrate analogue: substrate's structural-equivalence.

concepts.name: logical_consequence
concepts.definition: Q follows from P iff every model of P is model of Q. Substrate analogue: substrate's derivation relation.

concepts.name: consistency
concepts.definition: Set of propositions with simultaneous model. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherent Mt set.

concepts.name: proof
concepts.definition: Sequence of steps from premises to conclusion via inference rules. Substrate analogue: substrate's derivation chain.

concepts.name: axiom
concepts.definition: Proposition accepted without proof. Foundation of system. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded Rule.

concepts.name: theorem
concepts.definition: Proposition provable from axioms. Substrate analogue: substrate's derived Mt-content.

concepts.name: informal_logic
concepts.definition: Reasoning in natural language. Argumentation theory. Substrate analogue: substrate's everyday inference.

concepts.name: formal_logic
concepts.definition: Reasoning with formal language + precise rules. Substrate analogue: substrate's typed inference.

concepts.name: symbolic_logic
concepts.definition: Formal logic with symbolic notation. Substrate analogue: substrate's Term-tree representation.

rules.name: modus_ponens
rules.head: the substrate has P and P→Q
rules.body: it can conclude Q. Foundational deductive rule. Substrate's rule-firing pattern.

rules.name: modus_tollens
rules.head: the substrate has P→Q and ¬Q
rules.body: it can conclude ¬P. Contrapositive form. Substrate's denial-by-consequent.

rules.name: valid_argument_preserves_truth
rules.head: the substrate has a valid argument with true premises
rules.body: the conclusion must be true. Validity = truth-preservation. Substrate's sound inference.

rules.name: consistency_required_for_meaningful_inference
rules.head: the substrate's premise set is inconsistent
rules.body: anything follows (ex falso quodlibet). Inference becomes trivial. Substrate's coherence requirement.

rules.name: inductive_strength_depends_on_evidence
rules.head: the substrate generalizes from instances
rules.body: the inductive strength depends on sample size + representativeness. Inductive logic. Substrate's empirical confidence.
